title: Fixed-degree resultant counting with negative quadratic discriminant
difficulty_reason: The authors first reduce primitive negative-discriminant forms to fundamental discriminant via a change of variables, bound integer pairs represented by a reduced positive definite form, and use the cited Landesman correspondence to control the resulting form classes by n-torsion. A dyadic discriminant sum then imports the cited Koymans–Thorner torsion moment to give the power-saving bound; the second conclusion is explicitly conditional on the stated Cohen–Lenstra type average. The full counting argument, not just the final citation or a generic class-group bound, is retained.

readability.basis: Existing 12-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically viewed page 3 with Theorem 1.5 and prior hypothesis, and pages 10–11 with the complete authors’ counting lemma and theorem derivation.

dedup.scope: Current master title searches for resultant, quadratic class group, class group torsion and Browning–Chan; same-work published entry and arXiv alias examined by their actual primary statement.

compared.relation: Same publisher version Theorem 1.1 bounds quadratics with an odd-degree unit-resultant partner by B^3/sqrt(log B), without restricting to negative discriminant. Theorem 1.5 fixes the polynomial degree and requires negative discriminant, giving a power-saving bound and a separately conditional near-B^2 bound.
Earlier arXiv version of the same work, selected lemma lem:res2 is a determinant expression for the resultant; it does not assert the negative-discriminant counting bounds.

source_disclosures: The second conclusion depends on the explicitly stated class-group torsion average; it is not unconditional. The authors cite Koymans–Thorner for the n-torsion average and Landesman for the class-group correspondence.
